title: Ulpana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Eruvin 67a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.67a.14) has Rav Nachman bar Ami saying in the name of Ulpana; Hyman inserts that the first name should be Rav Chanin, as in Dikdukei Soferim and Yuchasin. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.67a.14.1) explains that he heard it from his teacher, whereas Yuchasin takes Ulpana as a sage’s name. Hyman cites [Dikdukei Soferim](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/-tMwzyO-dBEC?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA272) for the reading Ilfa. [Arakhin 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.28b.4) has Rabbi Chiya bar Abba saying in the name of Chulfana; Hyman suggests the reading Ulpana.[^3]

notes.text: The supplied בא אמי is read with Eruvin 67a בר אמי, bar Ami, rather than Ami came. Rashi’s teacher-term explanation and Yuchasin’s personal-name explanation remain alternatives. The proposed Chanin and Ilfa readings belong to Hyman’s cited witnesses.

The consulted Eruvin 67a reads Nachman bar Ami; Rashi explains a teaching heard from his teacher, whose teacher heard it from his teacher. The exact Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim variants remain Hyman’s reports here.

Rashi explains Ulpana as a teaching passed down by teachers. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=263&lang=en) also considers Ulpana a possible name. Dikdukei Soferim’s printed and manuscript columns show Nachman/Ulpana and Chanin/Ilfi, respectively. The Arakhin passage names Rav Chiyya bar Ami, where Hyman has Rabbi Chiya bar Abba. Heilprin also suggests reading Ulpana for Chulfana there.
